Accroches écrites : « Signs you're finally becoming disciplined » (retenue), « You're more disciplined than you think if… » (écartée : long), « Proof your habits are working » (écartée : vague).

slides.texte_overlay: You do things without negotiating with yourself. The alarm rings, you get up. The gym slot arrives, you go. The daily debate in your head is gone.
You feel strange when you skip a habit. Missing a workout or a reading session now feels off. That discomfort means the habit has become part of you.
You choose long-term over instant. The extra hour of sleep over the late scroll, the home meal over the delivery. Small choices show who's in charge.
You finish what you start. Books, courses, projects. Starting is easy. Finishing quietly is one of the clearest signs of real, lasting discipline.
Before: I gave up on every habit after a week. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a daily streak I've now kept for months.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I gave up on every habit after a week. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A streak I've kept for months.

slides.texte_overlay: You stop needing people to watch. You train hard alone, work well without a boss nearby. Discipline is what you do when nobody at all is checking.
You stay calm when plans break. A missed day doesn't ruin your week anymore. You simply adjust and keep going, because the habit is stronger than the setback.
